scenario.label: What the prospect actually needs
scenario.brief: We are in discovery with a prospect and I want our own side's read written down separately before we build the proposal, because we have twice now proposed the thing we wanted to sell rather than the thing they asked for.
scenario.theDecision: The two people in the room heard different problems: one heard a reporting problem, one heard a headcount problem. The buyer said the word "audit" three times and neither wrote it down. A right answer names the disagreement about what the customer actually said before any proposal is written.

people.name: Julia Fernandes
people.truth: She heard a reporting problem and has already sketched a dashboard proposal. She remembers the word audit but thought it was context. The deal is worth 90k.
people.manner: Confident, moves to solution quickly, will slow down when asked exactly what the customer said.

people.name: Martin Vogel
people.remit: Solutions engineer. Was in the same meeting.
people.truth: He heard a staffing problem: they cannot hire enough analysts. He also noted the buyer said "our auditors asked us for this" three times, which he thinks is the actual driver and the real deadline.
people.manner: Quiet, literal, quotes what people said rather than summarising it.
